questions.q: What makes Microsoft 365 Copilot different from a plain chatbot?
options: It's grounded in your own work data (mail, files, chats)
It works offline with no data
questions.explain: Copilot's edge is grounding — it answers using your tenant's real content, with citations, not just general knowledge.

questions.q: Your Copilot prompt returns a weak draft. Best improvement?
options: Add the audience, goal, tone, and a file to ground it
questions.explain: Specific, grounded prompts win. Point Copilot at the right document and tell it who it's for and what 'good' looks like.

questions.q: Copilot drafts an email citing a figure from a file. Before sending you should:
options: Open the cited source and confirm the figure
questions.explain: Citations make verification easy — actually click through and confirm before anything leaves your outbox.

questions.q: Which is a great everyday Copilot use?
options: Recapping a Teams meeting you missed with action items
questions.explain: Meeting recap with owners and actions is a classic high-value, low-risk Copilot task.

questions.q: A colleague worries Copilot will leak data to the public internet. The reassurance is:
options: It respects your existing permissions and stays in your tenant
questions.explain: Copilot honours the access controls you already have — it can't surface content a user couldn't already reach.

questions.q: Best mindset when Copilot writes a document for you?
options: Treat it as a fast first draft you edit and own
questions.explain: Copilot accelerates the first 80%. You still own the judgement, accuracy, and the final word.
